title: Engineering Solutions for Biological Studies of Flow-Exposed Endothelial Cells
author: Andreia Fernandes
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b2bwqape
materials: Sterilize with UV light for 15 minutes.

For endothelial cell monocultures: HUVECs were seeded on 0.2% gelatin-coated glass 6-well plates (Cellvis, P06-1.5H-N) with a cell density of 8×10 4 cells/cm 2 , using MCDB131 medium (Invitrogen) and a Low Serum Growth Supplement Kit (Invitrogen, S003K). After 1-3 days of static culture, the cell layer became confluent, and the plates were placed on an orbital shaker (VWR® Advanced 3500 Orbital Shaker, radius 9.5 mm), where the cells were exposed to pulsatile laminar flow in the periphery and disturbed flow in the center. To create wall shear stress values within the physiological range, the shaker velocity was set to 135 rpm, and 2 mL of culture medium were added to each well. After 3 days under flow conditions, cells had aligned with the flow and were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde for 15 min.

For co-cultures: HASMCs were seeded on 0.2% gelatin-coated glass 6-well plates with a cell density of 4×10 4 cells/cm 2 , using SmGM. After 3 days, HASMCs were stained with 10 µM CellTracker™ Green CMFDA Dye (Thermo Fisher, C7025) for 40 minutes at 37 °C. After 3 long washing steps with SmGM, HUVECs were seeded at 8×10 4 cells/cm 2 on top of the HASMCs, using MCDB131 medium (Invitrogen) and a Low Serum Growth Supplement Kit (Invitrogen, S003K). After 4 hours, the culture medium was exchanged and co-cultures were placed on the shaker. To create wall shear stress values within the physiological range, the shaker velocity was set to 135 rpm, and 2 mL of culture medium were added to each well. After 3 days under flow conditions, the cells were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde for 15 min.

Immunostaining and imaging: HUVECs were permeabilized for 10 minutes with 0.1% Triton and blocked with 1% BSA for 1 hour at room temperature. VE-cadherin antibody (Cell Signaling #2500, 1:500) and goat anti-rabbit antibody labelled with Alexa Fluor 488 (Invitrogen A11034, 1:250) diluted in 1% BSA were used. Incubation with primary antibodies was done overnight at 4° C and secondary antibodies for 1h at room temperature. EC monoculture images were made with a Nikon Eclipse Ti2 epifluorescence microscope using Nikon NIS-Elements Advanced Research 5.02 software. EC-SMC co-culture widefield fluorescent images were created in an ImageXpress micro (IXM) from Molecular Devices using Molecular Devices MetaXpress 5 software. Images were stitched into a large mosaic using JavaScript.

steps.title: Mark well centre
steps.instruction: Draw a cross to locate the centre of each well and mark a virtual circle with four points 6 mm from the well edge; for glass‑bottom plates place a sterile filtered 10 µL drop of 3‑(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate (TMSPMA) 1 % v/v in methanol in the centre.

steps.title: Place coverslip on TMSPMA
steps.instruction: Using sterile tweezers, place a sterilised 12 mm‑diameter glass coverslip directly on top of the TMSPMA droplet.

steps.title: Incubate TMSPMA
steps.instruction: Keep the plate at room temperature for 30 min, then incubate in a dry oven at 80 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Remove TMSPMA coverslip
steps.instruction: After cooling, fill the well with phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS), then gently lift off the coverslip with tweezers. (For plastic dishes the three steps above may be omitted.)

steps.title: Add PEG‑Irgacure solution
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of PEG‑Mw3400 (10 % w/v) containing 0.5 % w/v Irgacure 2959 (Material 55047962) dissolved in PBS to the centre of the well and cover immediately with a sterile 12 mm‑diameter coverslip.

steps.title: UV‑cure PEG hydrogel
steps.instruction: Expose the well to UV light for 30 seconds, then remove the coverslip while the well remains filled with PBS.

steps.title: Dry well
steps.instruction: Remove all PBS from the well and allow the surface to air‑dry.

steps.title: Gelatin coating
steps.instruction: Incubate the well with 0.2 % gelatin solution for 40 minutes at 37 °C.

steps.title: Wash gelatin
steps.instruction: Wash the well once with PBS.

steps.title: UV sterilise plate
steps.instruction: Expose the entire plate to UV light (duration as per laboratory standard) to sterilise the coated surface.

steps.title: Plate ready for cells
steps.instruction: The well is now ready for cell culturing on an orbital shaker; use a cell scraper for protein/RNA harvest, avoiding collection of the PEG coating.

steps.title: 3D‑print frame and pressing piece
steps.instruction: Print the locking frame and pressing piece from the provided STEP (*.stp) files using a Stratasys Eden 260VS printer with Vero Clear or Vero Black resin; the centring lugs deflect ≈0.25 mm inward and the pressing piece lower radius is ≈0.1 mm smaller than the well radius.

steps.title: Mold rubber gaskets
steps.instruction: Using machined Teflon templates, pour liquid PDMS (Sylgard® 184, Dow Corning) or Flexane (Devcon® Flexane 60L) into the template, avoid bubbles, place pre‑treated 50 mm × 50 mm × 1 mm glass slides (treated with 1H,1H,2H,2H‑perfluorodecyl‑trichlorosilane, ABCR) onto the resin, clamp with paper clips, cure overnight at 60 °C, then demould with a few drops of ethanol and tweezers.

steps.title: Obtain hardware components
steps.instruction: Acquire M4 × 9 mm stainless‑steel spring plungers and a retaining ring (OD 30.1 mm, thickness 1.2 mm) from standard hardware suppliers.

steps.title: Fabricate locking pieces
steps.instruction: Machine a 2.5 mm‑thick stainless‑steel ring (ID 29 mm, OD 35.15 mm), remove ≈0.3 mm of material from the outer circumference to sharpen one edge, then cut the ring into eight equal pieces using a 1 mm side‑milling cutter.

steps.title: Secure plate in mounting frame
steps.instruction: For glass‑bottom 6‑well plates, mount the plate into the provided mounting frame to prevent glass breakage when vertical force is applied; this step can be omitted for plastic‑bottom plates.

steps.title: Insert gasket into pressing piece
steps.instruction: Place the cured rubber gasket into the retainer of the pressing piece; optionally apply a thin layer of hydrophobic silicone paste to the gasket’s lower surface for improved sealing.

steps.title: Place pressing piece in well
steps.instruction: Remove any liquid from the well, then carefully insert the pressing piece (with gasket) directly onto the fixed cells, avoiding lateral movements.

steps.title: Load locking pieces and spring plungers
steps.instruction: Insert the four locking pieces into the retainers of the locking frame with the sharpened edge facing upwards; partially screw the spring plungers into the locking frame by hand.

steps.title: Compress retaining ring
steps.instruction: Using circlip pliers, compress the retaining ring so it fits into the groove inside the locking frame; this forces the locking pieces outward against the well wall, securing the insert.

steps.title: Tighten spring plungers
steps.instruction: Tighten the spring plungers with a screwdriver until a “click” is heard, then turn an additional half‑turn to achieve the final compression.

steps.title: Add staining reagents
steps.instruction: Immediately fill each compartment (≈100 µL per pocket) with the appropriate staining reagent; perform this step within ~1 minute, preferably after pre‑assembling all parts. Test for leakage with PBS before adding reagents.

steps.title: Post‑staining handling
steps.instruction: Leave the pressing piece in the well for imaging; removal of the locking frame may compromise the seal, so add extra liquid if needed. For long‑term storage, add PBS containing 0.01 % sodium azide.
